graph_decision.evidence: Analysis of the three axes reveals two distinct types of anomalies. 1) A permanent step change occurs at J1 (index ~587). This is clearly visible in the E-axis as a sharp drop from ~0 to -12 MAD, and in the U-axis as a jump from ~-1 to +1.5 MAD. The N-axis shows a corresponding upward shift. Since the level does not return to the previous baseline, this is classified as a standalone step (J1). 2) A transient spike occurs around indices 640-645. In the E-axis, there is a large negative excursion starting at J2 (~640) that returns to the new baseline at J3 (~645). The U-axis also shows a downward trend during this period. The candidate pair P3 (J2-J3) correctly identifies this short-duration anomaly where the signal shifts and then returns. Therefore, J2 and J3 are paired.
